stations.visualBrief: Long sectional assembly halls, repeated berths, common handling interfaces, mill steel structure and ochre service markings.
Dense standardized transfer spine with container, tanker and common-parts handling geometry; logistics reads as the hero function.
Modular clean precision blocks linked to common production interfaces, without ceremonial central citadel.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Speaks as Director of the Union Plant Council and head of state: capacity obligations, charter authority and inter-combine commitments are stated as measurable public responsibilities.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Balances regional works councils, fleet demand and civilian continuity; fears that over-centralized emergency allocation will turn commonality into a single political point of failure.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: As Central Capacity Board administrator, uses qualification, capacity and contract language with explicit industrial responsibilities.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Values measurable competence and continuity over prestige and guards reserve capacity against politically attractive overcommitment.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: As Fleet Production Defense commander, issues concise readiness, escort and production-network defense orders.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Treats fleet strength as inseparable from replaceable ships and intact flows, and prefers defensible throughput over prestige deployments.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Bulk tonnage, slots, route windows and reserve coverage.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Distrusts plans that ignore freight concentration and tanker exposure.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: As chief series-yard authority, speaks in line rates, tooling, changeovers, tolerances and common parts.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Proud of serial reliability and wary of bespoke emergency redesigns that strand tooling and spares.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: As infrastructure intelligence and anomaly liaison, reports only evidence-qualified route, site and production-network observations.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Focuses on failure propagation through shared hubs and common assemblies and suspects anomalous events are most dangerous when they mimic ordinary correlated failures.

recurringNpcs.publicVoice: Practical repair, access and delivery language from the frontier maintenance network.
recurringNpcs.privateVoice: Knows standardized fleets recover quickly only while common spares actually arrive and distrusts central plans that omit the last route segment.

missions.semanticIntent: Move finite common assemblies into a series-yard buffer through ordinary freight.
Procure finite bulk inputs for an active production series.
Protect real bulk traffic feeding concentrated industrial hubs.
Restore a named logistics group with finite reaction mass.
Obtain actor-bounded evidence around a threatened production corridor.
Recover finite salvage into ordinary industrial reuse.
Defend a concentrated supply corridor through an existing operation.
Deliver finite repair inputs to restore production infrastructure.
Resolve contracted market access through existing diplomacy authority.
Negotiate reciprocal emergency yard and market access for finite reserve capacity through ordinary diplomacy rather than granting scripted industrial access.
Assemble a maintainable standardized group and its logistics escort.

storyChains.semanticIntent: Political capacity commitment and contracted access become physical bulk flow that must survive real route risk before series production can continue.
Observed disruption becomes a real defensive operation followed by finite industrial repair rather than scripted recovery.

visualRules.requirement: Without color, every family must read through repeated sections, common engine banks and replaceable production modules rather than an Imperial central citadel.
Propulsion, service doors, sensor blocks, PD housings and handling interfaces visibly repeat across classes and industrial infrastructure.
Foundry graphite, mill steel, machine slate and assembly grey dominate; oxide ochre and safety amber mark service/handling functions with limited instrument teal and signal red.
Every character composes the canonical hand-painted Character Master style with the Industrial Union faction overlay, role brief and individual brief.
Status is legible through qualification, responsibility, equipment precision and material quality, never aristocratic costume or retro-Soviet cliché.
